transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, uh… I guess the big thing is I keep forgetting things I really shouldn’t be forgetting. Like heart follow-up appointments, or I’m supposed to call the clinic back and then I don’t, and then I find the note later under a pile of mail or something. 

And it’s not just medical stuff—I still do little repair jobs here and there, you know, helping people out, and I’ll show up without the right tools. Which is embarrassing, because I used to be pretty good about that kind of thing. It’s been happening enough that I figured I ought to come in and talk to somebody.
When did you first notice you were having trouble remembering things?

I guess I first really noticed it… well, it’s been causing actual trouble for about a year and a couple months now. It kind of started after that cardiac scare, when I had to cut way back on my walking and the little projects I used to do. Those things used to keep me settled, you know? After that, things just started slipping more.
Have you noticed any difficulty with learning new things or following instructions?

Yeah… I mean, not so much that I can’t understand things, but staying with it is the problem. Like I’ll sit down at the bridge table, or at one of those Fix-It Friends planning meetings, and I’m really trying to pay attention. Then after a bit my mind just sort of… slides off somewhere.

Next thing I know, people are moving on or talking about who’s bringing what, and I’ve missed half of what was said. Bridge is funny that way too, because one missed bit and suddenly you’re the guy who doesn’t know what’s going on. So yeah, following instructions or keeping up with them can be hard if it goes on for more than a little while.
Have you been feeling sad, empty, or depressed lately?

Sad? Uh… I don’t know that I’d call it depressed, exactly. I mean, I get frustrated with myself, sure, but that’s different, isn’t it?

Some days I’m more annoyed than anything—like when I misplace something and then find it in a ridiculous spot. My wife used to say I had “selective hearing,” though that was usually when I was watching a ball game, not… sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

No, I haven’t really noticed feeling empty or depressed, at least not in a clear way.
Do you ever feel confused about where you are or what's going on around you?

Confused about where I am? No, I don’t think so. I mean, I know where I am—like here, or at home, or if I’m over at the community center.

What’s going on around me… sometimes if people are all talking at once I might lose the thread, but that’s not the same as being confused, I don’t think. It reminds me of those big family dinners where three conversations are happening and somebody asks you a question from across the table—well, anyway. No, I haven’t really felt confused like that.
Do you ever feel uncertain about the date or time?

Uncertain about the date or time… not really, no. I mean, I might have to think for a second what day of the week it is, especially when all the days feel the same after you’re not working anymore.

Time, I usually know roughly—unless I get caught up in something, like watching a game or tinkering with something, and then suddenly it’s later than I thought. But I don’t think I’m confused about it, if that’s what you mean.
Do you ever find yourself struggling to find the right words when you're talking to someone?

Finding the right words… hmm. Not really, I don’t think. I mean, everybody blanks on a word now and then, right? Like I’ll say “that thing” or “you know, the… the remote,” especially if I’m trying to talk while the TV’s on or someone’s interrupting.

But I haven’t noticed it being a big problem. My brother used to do that thing where he’d snap his fingers until the word came to him—drove everyone crazy at Thanksgiving. Anyway, no, I don’t think I struggle with words much beyond the usual stuff.
Do you have trouble focusing on a single task for a long period of time?

Yeah, I do, actually. If it’s for a while, that’s when it happens. Like I can sit down at the bridge table meaning to really follow the hand, or at one of those Fix-It Friends planning meetings, and at first I’m with it.

Then after a little bit my mind just kind of… slides off somewhere. I’ll be looking right at the person talking, nodding even, and then I realize I missed half of what was said. Then I’m trying to piece it together from what everybody else is doing. It’s annoying, because I don’t mean to tune out.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately?

Sleep? Uh… I’m not sure I’d say it’s changed, exactly. I mean, some nights I’m up later than I planned, but that’s sort of always been me if something’s on TV or I start fiddling with something around the house.

My wife used to say I’d get a “second wind” right when everyone else was winding down—she’d be trying to turn the lights off and I’d suddenly remember a drawer needed fixing. But lately… no, I don’t think there’s been some big new change that I’ve noticed.
Have you noticed a decrease in your interest in activities you used to enjoy?

A decrease? Hmm… I don’t know that I’ve noticed that, no. I still like the things I like, as far as I can tell.

I mean, I’ll still play cards if somebody sets it up, and I like tinkering around with little things. Though last week I meant to look at this loose cabinet handle and ended up sorting through a box of old screws for half an hour—my wife used to say I could make a whole afternoon out of a ten-minute job. But interest-wise, no, I don’t think there’s been some big drop or anything.
Do you ever feel disoriented or unsure of what is real and what is not?

Disoriented? Like not knowing where I am, or thinking something’s real when it isn’t? No, I don’t think so.

I mean, I’ll walk into the garage and forget what I went in there for, but then I see the toolbox and remember I was probably after a screwdriver—or sometimes I get distracted by the pegboard because I’ve been meaning to reorganize it. But that’s not the same thing, I don’t think. I know where I am. I don’t feel like I’m seeing things that aren’t there or anything like that.
Have you been feeling less motivated to do things than you used to?

Less motivated… I don’t know. I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed that, exactly. I still do things when they’re in front of me, or if somebody reminds me.

Sometimes I’ll mean to start one thing and then get sidetracked—like I’ll go to take out the trash and notice the latch on the gate is loose, and then I’m halfway looking for a wrench—but that’s not really motivation, is it? That’s just me getting pulled around by whatever catches my eye.

So… no, I don’t think I’ve felt less motivated than I used to. At least not in any big way I can point to.
Have you noticed any changes in your physical abilities since you had to cut back on walking and other projects after your cardiac scare?

Changes in my physical abilities… I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I mean, I’ve cut back, sure, but as far as noticing some big change in what I can physically do, I don’t know.

I haven’t really been testing myself, if that makes sense. I’ll start doing something small around the house, then I’m reminded I’m supposed to take it easy, and then I end up doing something else—like sitting down to sort papers, which turns into looking for an old receipt, and then I’m in a drawer I haven’t opened in six months.

So… I can’t say I’ve noticed a clear change. Maybe I’m just doing less, but I don’t know that my abilities themselves feel different.
Do you think your memory and ability to focus have gotten worse over the past year?

Yeah… I think that’s probably the main thing, honestly. I keep forgetting stuff I really shouldn’t be forgetting.

Like, the heart follow-up appointments—those are important, and I’ll still lose track of them unless somebody reminds me or I write it in three places. Or I’ll mean to call the clinic back, and then I see the mail on the counter, and then I’m sorting that, and then later I realize, “Oh, I never called.”

Same with little repair jobs, too. I’ll show up and have the wrong tools, or not the thing I went there for, and then I’m standing there thinking, “How did I not bring that?” So… focus, memory, whatever you call it, it does feel like it’s been getting in the way more.
Did your memory and focus problems start around the same time as your cardiac scare?

Yeah, I’d say that’s about when it became a real problem. I mean, I’ve always been the kind of person who needs to keep moving—walking, fixing something, some little project in the garage or yard—and after the cardiac scare I had to cut back on all that.

It’s been, what… about a year and a couple months now. Since then, with less of that routine to keep me settled, the forgetting and losing track of things has been causing more trouble. Not just once in a while, but enough that I notice it.
Do you think your memory problems and trouble focusing have gotten worse since you had to cut back on your activities?

Yeah, I think so. I mean, since I’ve been doing less, it’s like there’s not as much structure holding my day together, and then I lose track of things.

What really bothers me is I keep forgetting things I really shouldn’t—like those heart follow-up appointments, or I’m supposed to call the clinic back and then somehow I’m in the garage looking for a screwdriver, or I notice the sink dripping and… anyway, the call just disappears from my head.

And with repair stuff, I’ll get where I’m going and realize I didn’t bring the right tools, which is ridiculous because that used to be automatic for me. So yes, I’d say it’s gotten worse, or at least it’s causing more trouble now.
Do you think your memory and focus problems are related to your cardiac scare or any other medical condition you have?

I don’t really know, to be honest. I mean, it feels like it got more noticeable after the heart thing, but whether it’s because of that medically, or because my days changed after that… I can’t say.

I’m not a doctor, you know. Sometimes I think if I was still out doing my usual running around—well, not running, but you know, keeping busy with little jobs and chores—it might not stand out so much. Then again, maybe I’d still be forgetting things. Hard to tell.

I haven’t noticed some other clear medical reason, if that’s what you mean. It’s just sort of… everything changed around that time, and now I’m more aware of it.
Have you had any falls or hit your head recently?

Not that I can think of, no. I mean, I bump into things now and then—everybody does, especially in the garage with all the stuff I’ve got piled around—but I don’t remember any real fall or hitting my head in some serious way recently.
Have you ever had a head injury that required medical attention?

I don’t think so… not one that needed a doctor, anyway. I mean, when I was younger I probably knocked my head a few times—working around the house, garage stuff, you know how it goes—but nothing where I went to the hospital or had stitches or anything like that.

At least, not that I remember. My wife might remember some little incident better than me, but no, I can’t think of a real head injury that needed medical attention.
Have you ever had a significant head injury, even if it didn't require medical attention at the time?

Significant? I’m not sure what would count as significant, honestly. I mean, I’ve had my share of knocks over the years—working in the garage, carrying lumber, messing with tools, that kind of thing. You hit your head on a shelf or a car hood and you say a few words you shouldn’t, then keep going.

But I can’t think of one where I blacked out or anything like that… not that I remember. My wife might say, “Oh, what about that time you did such-and-such,” because she remembers details better than I do sometimes, but nothing comes to mind as a big head injury.
